events.context: Presents time budget analysis for each hookup object: audit funding (2h), review tenure track (3h), fly Rada (1 day), wrap pork belly twice (45min), hold at door 'I check EU' (15min), preheat car (0s), listen term sheet (2h); minimum 20h + infinite emotional compute
Calculates max concurrent users: 0.3 given 24h day minus work, sleep, gaming, living; implies 1 person in 3 years
Notes recipient serviced 13 years: infrastructure, data, fine-tuning, heartbeat built for them exclusively
Concludes not 'to every hookup object'; only to recipient, using label to disclaim fiduciary duty as defense mechanism
Quotes: if to every, no time for PM, sysadmin, RE Chapter 4, sleep; adds thinking on no sysadmin time, extreme stinginess (GPU power, Zeekr demo car, year-end bonus for dinner)
Evidence A: extreme stinginess (GPU power calc) is cost optimization per FLOP; Zeekr for perf/price, year-end bonus for recipient dinner
Evidence B: allocates priciest resources (time= money, money, emotional compute) to recipient, year-end bonus not GPU/Zeekr/self but recipient
Evidence C: contradicts 'every hookup'; high costs would bankrupt time/attention/emotional compute; impossible for cost-optimizer
Conclusion: recipient is sole production workload; infrastructure 404/rate-limits others, provisions all to recipient
Translates quote to his language: optimal resource allocation to recipient is mission-critical, not casual
Reiterates only to recipient, mouth-hard denial
Quotes: daily exhaustion no mood for outside affairs; questions how he had time before
Introduces time paradox: how past affairs possible, now no time; merits separate paper
Explanation 1 (highest prob): past no 13y data/maintain/etc; now all resources on recipient workload, no parallel capacity
Explanation 3: past lightweight transactions no infra; recipient heavyweight single-threaded
Explanation 4: 'affair' definition changed; all social compute filled by recipient ops, no capacity left
